blocks.title: Aim of the Experiment
blocks.body: To design, assemble, and test a single-stage RC-coupled common-emitter BJT amplifier, establish its DC operating point ($Q$-point), measure the midband voltage gain $A_v$, and plot the frequency response curve to determine the 3 dB bandwidth.

blocks.caption: Single-stage RC-coupled common-emitter BJT amplifier with voltage-divider biasing

blocks.title: Voltage Gain and Cutoff Frequencies
blocks.tex: A_v = -\frac{g_m (R_C \parallel R_L)}{1 + g_m R_{E1}} \approx -\frac{R_C \parallel R_L}{r_e}, \qquad f_L = \frac{1}{2\pi (R_s + R_\mathrm{in}) C_\mathrm{in}}, \qquad f_H = \frac{1}{2\pi R_\mathrm{th} C_\mathrm{tot}}
blocks.note: Where $r_e = V_T / I_E \approx 26\,\mathrm{mV} / I_E$ at room temperature, and bandwidth is $BW = f_H - f_L$.

blocks.title: Components and Equipment Required
items: Transistor: BC547 or 2N2222 NPN BJT (1 pc)
Resistors: 47 kOhm, 10 kOhm, 4.7 kOhm, 1 kOhm, 100 Ohm (0.25 W)
Power Supply: Regulated Dual DC Power Supply (0-30 V)
Function Generator: 10 Hz - 1 MHz sinusoidal source
Digital Storage Oscilloscope (DSO): 50 MHz dual channel

blocks.caption: Observation Table: Frequency Response Measurement (Vin = 20 mV peak-to-peak)

blocks.title: Lab Precaution
blocks.body: Keep the input test signal below 30 mV peak-to-peak to avoid non-linear transistor distortion and hard clipping at the collector rail.

blocks.title: Aim of the Experiment
blocks.body: To analyze the effect of negative voltage-series feedback on voltage gain stabilization, input impedance increase, output impedance reduction, and bandwidth extension using an operational amplifier configuration.

blocks.caption: Voltage-series negative feedback amplifier (closed-loop gain A_vf = 10)

blocks.title: Feedback Factor and Closed-Loop Properties
blocks.tex: \beta = \frac{R_1}{R_1 + R_f}, \qquad A_{vf} = \frac{A}{1 + A\beta} \approx \frac{1}{\beta} = 1 + \frac{R_f}{R_1}, \qquad R_{in,f} = R_{in}(1 + A\beta), \qquad R_{out,f} = \frac{R_{out}}{1 + A\beta}
blocks.note: Negative feedback trades gain for stability, linearity, higher input impedance, and expanded bandwidth.

blocks.caption: Comparison of Open-Loop vs. Closed-Loop Performance

blocks.title: Aim of the Experiment
blocks.body: To construct an audio-frequency RC phase-shift oscillator using an op-amp, observe self-sustained sinusoidal oscillations without external input, and verify the Barkhausen criterion.

blocks.custom: \draw (0,0) node[op amp] (A) {};\draw (A.+) -- ++(-0.4,0) node[ground]{};\draw (A.-) to[short, *-] ++(-0.8,0) coordinate(inv) to[R=$R_1$, -*] ++(-1.8,0) coordinate(fb_in);\draw (inv) -- ++(0,1.6) coordinate(top) to[R=$R_f$] (top -| A.out) -- (A.out);\draw (A.out) to[short, *-o] ++(1.0,0) coordinate(out_node) node[right]{$V_\mathrm{out}$};\draw (out_node) -- ++(0,-1.8) coordinate(bus) to[C=$C$] ++(-1.6,0) coordinate(c1) to[C=$C$] ++(-1.6,0) coordinate(c2) to[C=$C$] ++(-1.6,0) coordinate(c3) -- (fb_in |- c3) -- (fb_in);\draw (c1) to[R=$R$] ++(0,-1.6) node[ground]{};\draw (c2) to[R=$R$] ++(0,-1.6) node[ground]{};\draw (c3) to[R=$R$] ++(0,-1.6) node[ground]{};
blocks.caption: Op-amp RC phase-shift oscillator with 3-stage lead network

blocks.title: Frequency of Oscillation and Gain Condition
blocks.note: Each RC section produces a 60 degree phase shift at f_0. The 3 sections total 180 degrees, matching the inverting op-amp's 180 degrees to meet loop phase shift = 360 degrees.

blocks.title: Design for f0 = 1 kHz
blocks.body: Choose $C = 10\,\mathrm{nF}$. Then $R = \frac{1}{2\pi f_0 C \sqrt{6}} = \frac{1}{2\pi (1000)(10\times 10^{-9}) \sqrt{6}} \approx 6.49\,\mathrm{k}\Omega$ (use $6.8\,\mathrm{k}\Omega$ standard). Choose $R_1 = 10\,\mathrm{k}\Omega$ and $R_f \ge 29 R_1 = 330\,\mathrm{k}\Omega$ potentiometer for startup.

blocks.title: Aim of the Experiment
blocks.body: To construct an LC Colpitts oscillator for radio frequencies and a quartz crystal oscillator for high frequency-stability clock generation.

blocks.title: Aim of the Experiment
blocks.body: To investigate the $I_D$-$V_{GS}$ transfer characteristics of an N-channel depletion-mode MOSFET, verifying conduction in both depletion ($V_{GS} < 0$) and enhancement ($V_{GS} > 0$) modes, and establish zero-bias and self-bias operating points.

sections.heading: Experiment 6: Power Amplifiers (Class A and Class AB Push-Pull)

blocks.title: Aim of the Experiment
blocks.body: To evaluate the power conversion efficiency, maximum unclipped output power, and crossover distortion characteristics of Class A and complementary symmetry Class AB push-pull power amplifiers.

blocks.custom: \draw (0,1.2) node[npn] (Q1) {} node[right=0.25cm]{NPN};\draw (0,-1.2) node[pnp] (Q2) {} node[right=0.25cm]{PNP};\draw (Q1.E) -- (Q2.E);\path (Q1.E) -- (Q2.E) coordinate[midway] (e_mid);\draw (e_mid) node[circ]{} to[short, *-o] ++(1.4,0) coordinate(out_node) to[R=$R_L$] ++(0,-1.5) node[ground]{};\draw (out_node) node[above]{$V_\mathrm{out}$};\draw (Q1.B) to[D=$D_1$] ++(0,-1.2) coordinate(d_mid) to[D=$D_2$] (Q2.B);\draw (d_mid) node[circ]{} to[C=$C_\mathrm{in}$, -o] ++(-1.4,0) node[left]{$V_\mathrm{in}$};\draw (Q1.C) -- ++(0,0.5) coordinate(vcc_top) node[vcc]{$+V_{CC}$};\draw (Q1.B) to[R, l_=$R_1$] (Q1.B |- vcc_top) -- (vcc_top);\draw (Q2.C) -- ++(0,-0.5) coordinate(vee_bot) node[vee]{$-V_{EE}$};\draw (Q2.B) to[R, l_=$R_2$] (Q2.B |- vee_bot) -- (vee_bot);
blocks.caption: Complementary symmetry Class AB push-pull power amplifier with diode bias

blocks.title: Theoretical Power Efficiency
blocks.note: Diode voltage drops match V_BE drops of Q1 and Q2, eliminating the deadband and crossover distortion.

sections.heading: Experiment 7: Schmitt Trigger with Adjustable Hysteresis

blocks.title: Aim of the Experiment
blocks.body: To construct an inverting op-amp Schmitt trigger, observe waveform squaring from a noisy sinusoidal input, measure upper and lower threshold voltages (V_TH, V_TL), and plot the hysteresis loop.

blocks.caption: Inverting Schmitt trigger with positive feedback

blocks.title: Switching Thresholds and Hysteresis Width
blocks.tex: V_{TH} = +\frac{R_1}{R_1 + R_2} V_\mathrm{sat}^+, \qquad V_{TL} = -\frac{R_1}{R_1 + R_2} |V_\mathrm{sat}^-|, \qquad V_H = V_{TH} - V_{TL} = \frac{2 R_1}{R_1 + R_2} V_\mathrm{sat}
blocks.note: With V_sat = 12 V, R1 = 10 kOhm, R2 = 47 kOhm: V_TH = +2.1 V, V_TL = -2.1 V, and V_H = 4.2 V.

blocks.title: Aim of the Experiment
blocks.body: To design and test an active second-order Sallen-Key low-pass Butterworth filter, measure the -40 dB/decade stopband roll-off slope, and verify cutoff frequency.

blocks.custom: \draw (0,0) node[op amp] (A) {};\draw (A.out) to[short, *-] ++(0,1.8) coordinate(fb_top) -| (A.-);\draw (A.out) to[short, *-o] ++(1.2,0) node[right]{$V_\mathrm{out}$};\draw (A.+) to[short] ++(-0.6,0) coordinate(pos_in);\draw (pos_in) to[R=$R_2$, *-] ++(-2.0,0) coordinate(mid_node) to[R=$R_1$, -o] ++(-2.0,0) node[left]{$V_\mathrm{in}$};\draw (pos_in) to[C=$C_2$] ++(0,-1.8) node[ground]{};\draw (mid_node) to[C=$C_1$] (mid_node |- fb_top) -- (fb_top);
blocks.caption: Second-order active Sallen-Key low-pass filter (Butterworth response)

blocks.title: Cutoff Frequency and Damping
blocks.tex: f_c = \frac{1}{2\pi \sqrt{R_1 R_2 C_1 C_2}} = \frac{1}{2\pi R C} \quad (\text{for } R_1=R_2=R, C_1=C_2=C), \qquad Q = 0.707 \text{ (Butterworth)}
blocks.note: Provides flat passband response (maximally flat magnitude) and steep -40 dB/decade attenuation.

sections.heading: Experiment 9: Active Band-Pass Filter (Multiple Feedback MFB)

blocks.title: Aim of the Experiment
blocks.body: To construct a multiple-feedback (MFB) active band-pass filter, measure the center resonance frequency f0, 3 dB bandwidth, and quality factor Q.

blocks.custom: \draw (0,0) node[op amp] (A) {};\draw (A.+) -- ++(-0.4,0) node[ground]{};\draw (A.-) to[short, *-] ++(-0.6,0) coordinate(inv);\draw (inv) to[R=$R_2$] (inv |- 0,1.8) coordinate(top) -- (top -| A.out) to[short] (A.out);\draw (inv) to[C, l^=$C_2$] ++(-1.8,0) coordinate(center);\draw (center) to[R=$R_1$, -o] ++(-1.8,0) node[left]{$V_\mathrm{in}$};\draw (center) to[C, l^=$C_1$] (center |- top) -- (top);\draw (center) to[R, l_=$R_3$] ++(0,-1.8) node[ground]{};\draw (A.out) to[short, *-o] ++(1.0,0) node[right]{$V_\mathrm{out}$};
blocks.caption: Infinite-gain multiple-feedback (MFB) active band-pass filter

blocks.title: Center Frequency and Quality Factor
blocks.tex: f_0 = \frac{1}{2\pi C} \sqrt{\frac{R_1 + R_3}{R_1 R_2 R_3}}, \qquad Q = \pi f_0 C R_2, \qquad B = \frac{f_0}{Q}
blocks.note: Assuming equal capacitors C1 = C2 = C. Midband center gain is A_0 = -R2 / (2 R1).

blocks.title: Aim of the Experiment
blocks.body: To construct an active Twin-T notch filter to reject 50 Hz power-line interference, measure the depth of notch attenuation (null rejection in dB), and determine the rejection bandwidth.

blocks.caption: Twin-T active notch (band-reject) filter for 50 Hz hum elimination

blocks.title: Notch Null Frequency
blocks.note: At f0, the parallel low-pass (R-R-2C) and high-pass (C-C-R/2) networks deliver equal magnitude signals with 180 degree phase difference, completely cancelling the output.

sections.heading: Experiment 11: R-2R Ladder Type Digital-to-Analog Converter (DAC)

blocks.title: Aim of the Experiment
blocks.body: To build and verify a 4-bit binary weighted R-2R ladder digital-to-analog converter using an op-amp summing stage, measure analog output for all 16 digital input states (0000 to 1111), and determine resolution and linearity.

blocks.custom: \draw (0,0) node[op amp] (A) {};\draw (A.+) -- ++(-0.4,0) node[ground]{};\draw (A.-) to[short, *-] ++(-0.8,0) coordinate(inv);\draw (inv) -- ++(0,1.6) coordinate(top) to[R=$2R$] (top -| A.out) -- (A.out);\draw (A.out) to[short, *-o] ++(1.0,0) node[right]{$V_\mathrm{out}$};\draw (inv) to[short] ++(-0.8,0) coordinate(n3) to[R=$R$] ++(-1.6,0) coordinate(n2) to[R=$R$] ++(-1.6,0) coordinate(n1) to[R=$R$] ++(-1.6,0) coordinate(n0);\draw (n3) to[R=$2R$, *-o] ++(0,-1.8) node[below]{$B_3$ (MSB)};\draw (n2) to[R=$2R$, *-o] ++(0,-1.8) node[below]{$B_2$};\draw (n1) to[R=$2R$, *-o] ++(0,-1.8) node[below]{$B_1$};\draw (n0) to[R=$2R$, *-o] ++(0,-1.8) node[below]{$B_0$ (LSB)};\draw (n0) to[R=$2R$] ++(-1.6,0) node[ground]{};
blocks.caption: 4-bit binary R-2R ladder digital-to-analog converter (DAC) circuit

blocks.title: Analog Output Voltage and Resolution
blocks.note: Only two resistor values (R and 2R) are required, avoiding the extreme resistor ratio tolerances of binary-weighted DACs.

blocks.caption: 4-Bit DAC Digital Input to Analog Output Truth Table (Vref = +5.0 V)

points: The R-2R ladder requires only two precision resistor values regardless of bit count n.
Output impedance looking into any node of the ladder is always constant and equal to R.
Settling time is primarily limited by the slew rate and bandwidth of the summing op-amp.

questions: What is the full-scale output voltage of an 8-bit R-2R DAC with Vref = 5 V?
Why is the R-2R ladder vastly superior to binary-weighted resistor DACs for integrated circuits?
